chapter: Opening, arrival in Los Angeles and the Quality Four
title: Giving Lionel Hampton his first band job at the Nightingale
summary: Howard says Hampton, then a drummer, worked with his band in 1925; Mrs. Howard recounts Hampton's arrest in Long Beach and how Howard got him out and into the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: What about Lionel Hampton?
I met him in -- it was about -- oh, he was -- it was quite a number of years after I -- later, yeah with Lionel.
I see.
Lionel didn't have anything. He didn't -- she's got it.
(Recording interruption)
Okay, the last question was about when you met Lionel or when he worked with you or when you worked with him. Do you remember some of those days?
Well, yes, he worked with me at the -- 1925. That's when he worked with me.
Was he playing vibes at that time, or just playing drums?
Playing drums.
Only drums, not vibes.
No, wasn't playing vibes. I don't remember whether he was playing vibes or not. I can't remember.
I had heard stories that he was mostly a drummer in the beginning.
It sounded like he played vibes later, but (inaudible)
Yeah.
Was it your band he joined, or you just happened to be playing --
It was my band.
And do you remember what club you were working in?
Wasn't working at a club, we were just playing -- practising at the -- oh, it was the Nightingale.
Why don't we let Mrs. Howard and Mr. Howard talk about it for a minute?
That's why you're here.
Okay, would you take the microphone? Mr. Howard gave Lionel And you said that Mr. Hampton --
Lionel his first job.
-- his first job.

He went to Long Beach and brought up a band. (See, Les Hite and Lionel, George Orendorff -- he's a trombone player (Inaudible) and Louis (inaudible)) on the circuit, and some woman, brought them out here. He was just a young boy,
see. And they were playing a date there in Long Beach. And Lionel got into a little trouble (inaudible).
That's fine, you're doing just fine.
You're giving us some good information,
yes.
That's right. You tell us the things you remember, and then you'll probably remind him of more things.

So at the time, George (Brendorff) was he told Paul about Lionel with Paul playing at the Nightingale. And (inaudible), and they were rehearsing at the time to go into this embassy. I forget the fellow's name that opened it, but that was one of the high class places (inaudible).
So it would be in Hollywood.
Yes, it was in Hollywood. And George and Paul went down to Long Beach, on a Sunday, and Lionel was they had Lionel (inaudible) in jail. He was arrested.
Yeah, I remember that. so they got him out and brought him back to the city and that's when Lionel joined Paul's band.
